course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 9

unit.title: Position and transformation
unit.blurb: Bearings and scale drawings, midpoints and points dividing a line segment, combined transformations and enlargement.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Use bearings (three figures, measured clockwise from north) and scale drawings, including back bearings.

O2.t: Find the midpoint of a line segment and the point that divides it in a given ratio.

O3.t: Describe and carry out reflections, rotations and translations, including combinations.

O4.t: Enlarge shapes using a positive scale factor and a centre; find scale factors and centres.

p: A **bearing** is an angle measured **clockwise from north**, written with **three figures**: 045°, 230°.
The **back bearing** (from B back to A) is the bearing **± 180°**.

lesson.q: The bearing of B from A is 065°. Find the bearing of A from B.

p: A scale such as **1 cm : 5 km** means every 1 cm on the drawing is 5 km in real life. Multiply to get the real length; divide to get the drawing length.
A bearing of 45° is written 045°. Always measure from NORTH and go CLOCKWISE.

p: The **midpoint** of (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is **((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2)** – the mean of the coordinates.

lesson.q: Find the midpoint of A(1, 2) and B(7, 6).

p: To find P on AB with **AP : PB = m : n**, go the fraction **m/(m + n)** of the way from A: P = A + m/(m + n) × (B − A).
For AP : PB = 1 : 3, P is 1/4 of the way along, not 1/3.

p: **Reflection**: give the mirror line (e.g. y = x). **Rotation**: give the **angle, direction and centre**. **Translation**: give the **column vector** (right, up).
Reflections and rotations keep size and shape: the image is **congruent**.

p: An **enlargement** changes size but not shape. Every length is multiplied by the **scale factor**.
From the **centre of enlargement**, each image point is scale factor × as far away, in the same direction. Image = centre + k × (point − centre).
If lengths are multiplied by k, **areas are multiplied by k²**.
Doubling lengths does NOT double area – it multiplies area by 4.
